clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs change the same `if isinstance(data_value, str) and ...` guard in pre_parse_json to stop treating str-containing unions as always-parseable. #2032 introduces `_should_pre_parse_json`, which generalizes the fix to any union whose non-str members are all simple/pydantic-coercible types (str, int, float, bool, NoneType) — so it also correctly skips pre-parsing for str|int, str|float, str|bool, not just str|None. #3056's `_is_optional_str` only special-cases the exact str|None (Optional[str]) pattern, so str|int or str|bool annotations would still be incorrectly JSON-parsed under that fix. #3056 does add `_unwrap_annotated` to strip `Annotated[...]` wrapping from union args, which #2032's `arg in _SIMPLE_TYPES` membership check does not handle — but this covers a narrower edge case (Annotated-wrapped members inside a union) than the core bug both PRs target, so #2032's broader coverage of the root cause makes it the better base to keep; the Annotated-unwrap handling from #3056 can be folded into it if needed.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs change the same `if isinstance(data_value, str) and ...` guard in pre_parse_json to stop treating str-containing unions as always-parseable. #2032 introduces `_should_pre_parse_json`, which generalizes the fix to any union whose non-str members are all simple/pydantic-coercible types (str, int, float, bool, NoneType) — so it also correctly skips pre-parsing for str|int, str|float, str|bool, not just str|None. #3056's `_is_optional_str` only special-cases the exact str|None (Optional[str]) pattern, so str|int or str|bool annotations would still be incorrectly JSON-parsed under that fix. #3056 does add `_unwrap_annotated` to strip `Annotated[...]` wrapping from union args, which #2032's `arg in _SIMPLE_TYPES` membership check does not handle — but this covers a narrower edge case (Annotated-wrapped members inside a union) than the core bug both PRs target, so #2032's broader coverage of the root cause makes it the better base to keep; the Annotated-unwrap handling from #3056 can be folded into it if needed.

members.cluster_pick_reason: #2493 only removes the erroneous response send for the peer-initiated path (message.cancelled in server.py's _handle_request) - after this fix the peer that cancelled is simply never answered at all in the other trigger paths. #2514 imports CancelledNotificationParams and rebuilds cancel() to actively send a notifications/cancelled message on request timeout and caller-initiated cancellation, not just suppressing output for the peer-cancelled case. It's a strict superset: it fixes the same spec violation #2480 describes while also covering the timeout/caller-cancellation paths that #2493's diff never touches, so merging #2493 afterward would just be reverted by #2514's rewrite of the same function.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs edit the identical lines in utils.py to add `from e`, so they will conflict on merge regardless of which lands first. #2565 makes a narrowly-scoped change that only appends `from e` and leaves the existing f-string error messages (`f"Invalid registration response: {e}"`) untouched, minimizing diff size and avoiding any change to user-facing exception text. #2777 bundles in an additional edit that rewrites those same messages to drop the interpolated `{e}` (e.g. to `"Invalid registration response"`), which is an unrelated behavior/text change riding along with the chaining fix and increases the chance of breaking any test or caller that asserts on the exact exception message string.
